title: The mother's request for seats in the kingdom
english: About the request of the mother of the sons of Zebedee. The mother of the sons of Zebedee—whom the Savior called Boanerges—came forward and was asking that one should sit at his right side and one at his left in his kingdom. To those who cannot seek depths, the request seems like simplicity; but to those deeper, Jesus' answer also indicates something great. Just as in a worldly kingdom those who sit with the king are honored, so the two apostles, still being imperfect, supposed about the kingdom of Christ. But Jesus says, "You do not know what you are asking" (Matthew 20:22), and "It is not mine to give, but it is for those for whom it has been prepared by my Father" (Matthew 20:23).

title: What sitting at the right and left means
english: We must ask what the sitting at the right or at the left of Jesus in the kingdom means. The passages written about the throne of God or of Christ must be gathered together. In Kingdoms, Micaiah saw the Lord sitting on a throne. In Isaiah, “I saw the Lord sitting on a high throne” (Isaiah 6:1). In Daniel, “until thrones were set, and an Ancient of Days sat down” (Daniel 7:9). In the Psalm, “Sit at my right hand” (Psalm 110:1). And in the Gospels, “when the Son of Man sits on the throne of his glory” (Matthew 25:31). Perhaps the right side means the intelligible and invisible created things, and the left side the visible and bodily ones, and Christ rules over all. Glory to Christ. Amen.
